description: Contract automatically renews unless the tenant/party actively cancels within a narrow window.
why_it_matters: Can lock you into another full term if you miss a short opt-out window, sometimes with no reminder from the other party.

description: Landlord/company can raise rent or fees during the term, or on renewal, with minimal notice.
why_it_matters: Removes cost predictability; check the notice period and any caps.

description: Late payment fees that are flat-rate large amounts or compound daily without a cap.
why_it_matters: Can turn a small missed payment into a large one quickly.

description: Clause where the signer waives a legal right, e.g. right to a jury trial, right to sue, or class-action participation.
why_it_matters: Limits your legal options if a dispute happens later; often not obvious on a first read.

description: Signer agrees to cover the other party's legal costs/damages, but not vice versa.
why_it_matters: Puts financial risk asymmetrically on you.

description: Disputes must go to private arbitration instead of court.
why_it_matters: Arbitration can favor the party that uses the arbitrator repeatedly (usually the company/landlord) and limits appeal options.

description: Large flat fee or 'remaining balance of the term' owed if you need to exit early.
why_it_matters: Can be disproportionate to actual damages the other party incurs; worth negotiating a cap.

description: Vague or broad conditions under which a deposit can be withheld, or no stated return timeline.
why_it_matters: Ambiguous 'normal wear and tear' language is a common source of deposit disputes.

description: Blanket prohibition on subletting or assigning the agreement, sometimes even in emergencies.
why_it_matters: Limits flexibility if your situation changes (job relocation, needing a roommate, etc.).

description: Tenant/signer made responsible for repairs that are normally the landlord's/owner's duty (structural, major systems).
why_it_matters: Can create unexpected large costs; check local landlord-tenant law for what's typically non-shiftable.

description: What counts as a 'default' or 'breach' is defined broadly or left to one party's sole discretion.
why_it_matters: Gives the other party wide latitude to declare a breach and trigger penalties.

description: One party can change the terms of the agreement during the term without the other party's consent.
why_it_matters: Undermines the certainty of what you originally agreed to.
